Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

combination noun

also a combination of, in combination with, a mixture of

classical

Cic. Fin. 5.67: conjūnctiō virtūtum (Lewis & Short)

conjūnctiō, conjūnctiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a joining together, union, combination

Lewis & Short: rare of physical things; in good prose of joining things in the mind, and of bonds between people (friendship, marriage, kinship). In grammar it is a conjunction. Where English says “a combination of A and B”, Latin often says A cum B conjūnctum.

Other words

  • mixtūra (mistūra), mixtūrae f. — a mixing, a mixture

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Petr. 94: rāram facit mixtūram cum sapientiā fōrma (Lewis & Short); Col. 12.59.1: hanc mixtūram

    (ante-classical and post-Augustan (Lewis & Short))

    Lewis & Short’s headword is mistūra. For ingredients, colours, qualities; Lewis & Short also records a sexual sense (Luc., Plin.).

Examples

  • rāram facit mixtūram cum sapientiā fōrma

    beauty is rarely found in combination with wisdomPetr. 94 (Lewis & Short)

  • hanc mixtūram cum in catillō composueris, oleum superfunditō

    when you have put this mixture in a bowl, pour oil over itCol. 12.59.1

  • bene enim majōrēs accubitiōnem epulārem amīcōrum, quia vītae conjūnctiōnem habēret, convīvium nōmināvērunt

    our ancestors did well to call friends’ dining together a convivium, because it is a joining of livesCic. Sen. 45

See also mix, join, connect.

SourcesLewis & Short: conjunctio · Lewis & Short: mistura · Lewis & Short: conjungo

Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cato (Columella), loci-cicero-philosophica), checked against the editions named there.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
